chapter: Carnivals, Kansas City and the road to Chicago
title: Back in Des Moines: teaching Bill Fulton and the idea of Chicago
summary: Back in school, Barefield played around town on a borrowed C melody and gave jazz saxophone lessons to Chicagoan Bill Fulton. Fulton urged him to move to Chicago.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: But I wasn't happy, I wanted to play. I didn't have a horn, so I borrowed a C melody saxophone from a friend of mine and I played around Des Moines all that winter with this horn. And there was a friend of mine from Chicago who lived in Des Moines and he was home visiting. Came home Christmas

to visit his family, named Bill Fulton. And he wanted me to teach him how to play jazz on the saxophone. So I was giving him lessons, teaching him the way I played. And he said, what are you doing staying around Des Moines for? You should be in Chicago, he says, "much as you play," you know. Of course, the only thing that reading hadn't come in our minds, so we were saying interested -- we were interested, just playing -- improvising.
